question.text: Will the CBRT's November 2026 Financial Stability Report devote a dedicated box to the 2026 fund liquidations?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the basis of the English-language edition of the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye's Financial Stability Report scheduled for publication on 27 November 2026, accessible from the CBRT's 2026 Financial Stability Report page (https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Publications/Reports/Financial+Stability+Report/2026) through its "Click For Full Text" and "Cover Page, Foreword and Contents" links. It resolves YES if that report's table of contents lists at least one numbered box — any "Box" label format counts, e.g. "Box II.1", "Box III.1.I" or "Box IV.5" — whose title explicitly refers to the liquidation or winding-up of investment funds, to the Capital Markets Board (SPK)'s September 2026 action, or to the funds placed in liquidation. It resolves NO if no box title makes such a reference, including where the liquidations appear only in a chapter's body text or inside a box with a different title.
question.fine_print: A box whose title refers to investment funds generally, without referring to the liquidation, to the SPK's September 2026 action, or to funds placed in liquidation, does not count toward YES. If publication is delayed beyond 27 November 2026, resolution waits for the report to appear; the Turkish-language edition of the same report may be used if the English edition is unavailable. If the CBRT does not publish a November 2026 edition of the Financial Stability Report by 31 December 2026, the question is annulled.

research:
I couldn't find anything that settles this yet, and the evidence I did find leans against YES on the wording test. In its 12 November 2026 Inflation Report, the CBRT gave the fund crisis a box but titled it **"Recent Developments in Mutual Funds"**. That title doesn't mention liquidation. Under the fine print, the same title in the FSR would resolve NO.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: The CBRT's 2026 FSR page lists only "Financial Stability Report - May 2026, Volume 42". The November edition is not posted yet. [CBRT FSR 2026](https://tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Publications/Reports/Financial+Stability+Report/2026)
- The CBRT's English report pages link a "Full Text" PDF and a "Cover Page, Foreword and Contents" PDF. For past editions, box titles are listed only inside those PDFs, not on the web page. [FSR Nov 2025, Vol. 41](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Publications/Reports/Financial+Stability+Report/2025/Volume+41/)
- 2026-11-27: Scheduled release date, per the question.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The report is unpublished and I found no preview of its contents.
- 2026-11-12: Inflation Report 2026-IV has six boxes. One is "Box 2.2 Recent Developments in Mutual Funds". The others cover outright purchases, bank heterogeneity, firm interviews, export market share and mortgage debt. The Turkish title, as given in a search summary I could not open, is "Kutu 2.2 Yatırım Fonlarında Son Dönem Gelişmeler". This shows the CBRT is willing to box the episode, but it named it with a general "investment funds" title. [IR 2026-IV Boxes](https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Publications/Reports/Inflation+Report/2026/Inflation+Report+2026+-+IV/Boxes/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: Finance Minister Şimşek gave an update on the liquidations, reported as TRY 161 billion in payments to investors. [haberler.com](https://www.haberler.com/haberler/bakan-simsekten-milyonlarca-emekliyi-ilgilendiren-20429765-haberi/)
- 2026-11-12: Presenting the Inflation Report, Governor Karahan said the CBRT took steps to limit contagion from the investment-fund market, and that outflows went mostly into deposits. [Foreks/AA](https://www.foreks.com/haber/detay/6af58e74635b284a64306e1a/AA/tr/yenileme-3-tcmb-baskani-karahan-yatirim-fonu-piyasasinda-yasanan-gelismelerin-yayilma-riskini-sinirlamak-icin-adimlar-attik-12-11-26/)
- 2026-11-06: Karahan said contagion risk is limited for now. The CBRT raised funding through its weekly repo auctions and is ready to take more measures. [NTV](https://www.ntv.com.tr/turkiye/karahandan-fon-mesaji-gelismeler-yakin-takibimizde-1749721)
- 2026-11-04: A CBRT staff blog, "Fund Liquidations and the Real Sector", put real-sector firms' holdings in the affected funds at TRY 116 billion. [Bloomberg HT](https://www.bloomberght.com/fon-gelismelerin-reel-sektor-uzerindeki-etkisi-tcmb-arastirmacilari-inceledi-3793380)
- 2026-10-14: Karahan said outflows from the funds had not weakened residents' preference for the lira. [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/business/economy/turkish-lira-preference-remains-strong-despite-fund-outflows-cbrt)
- 2026-10-06: Karahan said "we are at the start of the liquidation process" and that over USD 16 billion had moved into deposits. Separately, the Justice Minister reported 85 arrests in the manipulation probe. [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/business/economy/over-16b-shifted-into-deposits-amid-fund-exits-turkish-central-bank/amp); [Milliyet](https://www.milliyet.com.tr/haber/7675300/)
- 2026-09-17 onward: The SPK ordered 131 funds liquidated, with İşbank and Ziraat Bank appointed to run it. The Financial Stability Committee said there was "no structural risk". The CBRT announced liquidity measures. [Milliyet](https://www.milliyet.com.tr/haber/7662642/); [Fintables](https://fintables.com/arastirma/yazilar/fonlar/fon-piyasasinda-yeni-donem-hangi-tedbirler-neyi-degistiriyor.md)

## 4. Base rates
- FSR 2026-I (May 2026) had six boxes, none in Chapter V (non-bank financial sector). Box IV.5 was titled in general terms ("financial-market measures"), per the question background.
- After the March 2025 turmoil, MNI reported that the May 2025 FSR covered it, finding limited financial-stability impact. I could not read that edition's contents PDF, so I can't confirm whether a box title named the event. [MNI](https://www.mnimarkets.com/articles/mni-brief-finstab-impacts-of-recent-turmoil-limited-cbrt-1748592945115)
- The closest precedent is the Inflation Report two weeks earlier. The CBRT boxed the topic but used neutral wording, consistent with its messaging that contagion is limited.
- The real-sector blog title did name "Fund Liquidations", so CBRT staff have used the explicit term in at least one publication.
- How likely a box is at all: the topic is extremely salient, and in May 2026 the FSR already flagged non-banks as 26% of the financial system. The open question is the title wording, not whether the topic gets covered.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this question. The markets supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) are unrelated; the closest, CAATSA sanctions on Turkey, has nothing to do with the FSR.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-27: FSR 2026-II publication, likely with a press briefing by the Governor.
- The liquidation process, extended to six months on 20 September, runs until about March 2027. Further SPK payment decisions are possible before 27 November.
- 2026-12-10: Next MPC rate decision, which falls after resolution.

**Caveat:** The PDFs I tried to open (Inflation Report full text, May 2025 FSR contents) came back as unreadable binary, so I only verified the English box titles listed on the CBRT web page.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. The FSR is due on 27 November 2026. For YES, its table of contents must list at least one numbered box whose title explicitly refers to the liquidation or winding-up of funds, to the SPK's September 2026 action, or to the funds placed in liquidation.

(b) If nothing changes, the report has no qualifying box title. The report is unpublished, and the CBRT's most recent framing (the Inflation Report box) uses generic "investment funds" wording, which would not count.

(c) Base rate: the FSR runs about 6 boxes per edition and usually boxes major topical shocks. I put the chance that the fund episode gets a box at all at roughly 80-90%. The binding constraint is title wording. CBRT box titles tend to be thematic ("Recent Developments in...", "Financial-Market Measures") rather than naming the event. Among comparable "topic boxed" cases, I estimate explicit naming of the event at roughly 30-40%. That gives a starting point of about 30-35%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For YES:**
  - The CBRT staff blog of 4 November 2026 was titled "Fund Liquidations and the Real Sector", so the institution has used the explicit term.
  - This is the largest fund crisis in Turkish history, and the FSR is the natural venue for a dedicated deep-dive.
  - Chapter V had no box in May 2026, which leaves room for one.
  - Governor Karahan has spoken openly of the "liquidation process" (8 October).
- **For NO:**
  - Inflation Report 2026-IV (12 November) boxed the topic as "Recent Developments in Mutual/Investment Funds", a generic title that would fail the test.
  - The CBRT's messaging stresses containment and a neutral tone.
  - The FSR has a pattern of thematic titles.

(e) Scenarios:
- **NO:** The FSR includes "Box V.1 Recent Developments in Investment Funds and Their Implications for Financial Stability", or covers the episode only in the Chapter V text.
- **YES:** The Financial Stability department titles a box "Assessment of the Fund Liquidation Process and Its Effects on the Financial System", echoing the blog's wording.

(f) I start at about 33%. The Inflation Report title, written two weeks earlier by the same institution, is the most direct precedent and points to generic wording, so I move down a few points. The blog's explicit title and the fact that the FSR is written by a different department keep the estimate from going much lower. I land at about 27%.

Probability: 27%
